newsitem.title: UK: UK's Clarke - Firms can transfer PFI stakes.
newsitem.headline: UK's Clarke - Firms can transfer PFI stakes.

text.p: Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke on Monday announced measures which will allow UK companies to transfer stakes in private finance initiative (PFI) projects.
The move should inject greater liquidity into PFI projects.
"It will increase the availability of capital for PFI investment. It will make the PFI more liquid. Above all, it will improve value for money," Clarke told a conference on the PFI in London.
Clarke once again said that the PFI was not a substitute for capital expenditure by the government.
"PFI is an alternative way of financing which offers value for money," Clarke said, adding that the two are complementary.
Clarke was speaking at the private finance annual conference where he sought to address some of the criticisms made by the UK construction industry and its financial backers.

The move to allow transfer of stakes will enable British firms to sell on their investments, rather than being locked in for the full 20-30 year PFI term. Clarke also said a standard set of contract terms would be introduced for PFI projects.
A total of seven billion stg has been committed to PFI projects this year, compared with 1.5 billion at the same stage last year.
"We have listened, we have learned. We are taking action," Clarke said. "PFI is a revolution in the provision of public services....after the revolution comes evolution."
